quotes.text:
AI has the potential to enrich our lives, but it also has the potential to do great harm without proper guardrails.

I joined @NEInstituteTech for their annual AI Summit to discuss how we can work to create smart guardrails that leave room for innovation while mitigating risks. https://t.co/csIn6HdiLo

AI technology is being used to misinform voters, cause confusion and spread dangerous lies. We need to address this issue for the sake of our democracy.

That’s why I am calling on @FEC to clarify rules around AI and deep fakes in order to combat misinformation. READ: https://t.co/VCKVRyJvO2

Kudos to @SecMayorkas and the Department of Homeland Security for making DHS one of the first federal agencies to make recommendations for how to use AI to improve operations.

Smart use of AI can help protect Americans from terror attacks, natural disasters, and other threats. https://t.co/GrSVh3RYTq

Rhode Island is the Saudi Arabia of offshore wind.

Blocking clean energy from the grid kills American jobs, raises Americans’ electric bills, and is a great way to lose the AI race to China. https://t.co/D1ynU6buxT

Today I joined the @BryantUniv Global Trade Summit, New England’s premier conference on international trade.

We discussed AI, U.S. trade policy, and how Rhode Island can attract investment, grow exports, and stay competitive in the global economy. https://t.co/Dbs25ZzWkR

The Chinese government just launched the first-ever AI-powered cyber attack against our country that we know of. At the same time, President Trump is selling the powerful H200 Nvidia chips, the next generation chips, to China. [...] Why in the world, given that they just did this, what, a couple months ago, would we be giving them these next generation chips now? At the very least, we ought to be holding them back until we have some way of verifying that these chips are not going to be used to attack us.

what regulation is required to ensure that commercially-available AI products have adequate guardrails in place? We appreciate the, you know, the efforts that companies are already undertaking, but there should be some sort of a baseline of standards that we set as a country, should there not?

I don't know how anybody can be okay with this chip sale, given what literally just happened two months ago. And that is something that I think we need to find a way as a Congress to deal with because the administration, I fear, has made a grave mistake.

China just launched the first ever AI-powered cyber attack against the U.S.

And Donald Trump just announced a deal to sell China the most advanced chips that power AI.
 
I asked four leading cybersecurity experts if they think this is a good idea. Spoiler alert: they don’t. https://t.co/Ji3KoYUNpo

Anthropic’s policies are very reasonable. 

The Pentagon should not be using AI to engage in mass surveillance of US citizens or power weapons that launch without a human operator.

Hegseth should back down. https://t.co/uxEtfCdo5k

Reminder, this is all because Anthropic does not want their product to be used in mass surveillance of Americans or to give their AI the power fire weapons with no human operator.

Where are all of my small government conservative colleagues in Congress on this? https://t.co/gSAUWdSUcs

I met w/ @sagaftra President & college football legend 😂 @SeanAstin at the Labor Caucus to talk about protecting workers in the entertainment industry.

From fair wages to protecting people’s image & likeness being copied by AI, we have to make sure artists are treated fairly. https://t.co/HE1lG1kLwo

This is something I have been calling for on the Cyber Subcommittee. As AI models become more powerful, there needs to be an independent process to test each new model for safety before public release. https://t.co/VzxoFF7WLD

At this morning’s @ProvChamber Congressional Dialogue Breakfast, I joined my colleagues in the Delegation to discuss the need to end the unnecessary tariffs and wars, support career & tech education, and be proactive in meeting the challenges of the AI age. https://t.co/PvMbGPcpGr

AI companies can accept secret money from drug companies to influence medical advice given to you, with no transparency.

That must change. I called on the FTC to require chatbots and search engines to disclose sponsorships with companies that influence answers in real-time. https://t.co/NGnxgswf8O

Millions use AI tools for product recommendations, research, and advice.

But these tools are not required to say if commercial interests influence the information you receive.

I just introduced a bill to make AI companies disclose sponsored content that impacts results. https://t.co/ZXTqmgFV1s

Americans deserve to know if the information they are getting is the best available, or if it is being manipulated to serve the interests paid sponsors. I am proud to introduce the AI Advertising Disclosure Act to ensure Americans know when and how advertising is influencing the information they receive from artificial intelligence.

Your AI search results include paid ads, and you may never know it.

That’s because FTC disclosure rules for TV, radio and social media don’t apply to AI.

My bill would close this loophole and ensure you know when a company is paying to influence your results. https://t.co/fZwfABTCWx
Everyone is talking about AI insiders saying their technology is a threat to humanity. Here is what Congress can do about it. https://t.co/sTFvQ2WVmq
the US government needs a transparent and mandatory policy for testing frontier models.

This is the White House AI tsar spinning out because the leaders of the largest AI companies are admitting that their technology is dangerous and needs to be regulated.

Regulate them! This is your job! What an epic failure of leadership, and the consequences could be devastating https://t.co/pdlMchgPcU

AI will get out of control if America doesn’t set the standard.

I joined 40 colleagues in asking President Trump to initiate global negotiations to build safeguards and avert disaster. https://t.co/E99LJIunDx

We’re seeing the risks of the AI race unfold in real time. Selling advanced AI chips to China would make those risks worse.  

I’m joining 14 of my colleagues in urging President Trump: Do not sell advanced American AI chips to the Chinese government. https://t.co/mHjYv1Is7r
Here’s the truth about why we don’t have AI safety standards: https://t.co/x81rZyeSS6

Data center developers should bear the full responsibility for their costs to connect to the grid and any needed impact mitigation. I support requiring data centers to be transparent about their impact on the public grid, the extent to which they will raise electricity rates for everyday homeowners and business owners, their demand on local water supplies, and the environmental impact they will have on the areas in which they are built so that local governments may make the best decisions for their residents.
The White House just released a new AI feature on its website, so I decided to ask it a few questions… https://t.co/vAHOCOgc3t
